the chandelier crash in Leroux's Le fantome de l'Opera and in its screen adaptations is a key moment in the history of cinema and of opera, and that the chandelier scene in the 1925 silent film version of the novel is an early and highly influential instance of the cinematic performance of opera, a genre of screen adaptations that would be developed and perfected in the 1930s and 1940s by Max Reinhardt, Michael Powell, and others.

the performance of cinema as a means of understanding the performance of opera in film, a performance that is not merely a matter of representation, but one of appropriation, of the screen's capacity to take over, to appropriate, the stage.

the chandelier crash is the ultimate performance of cinema.

the chandelier is a metaphor for cinema.
